title: Optimal Arms Identification with Knapsacks
motivation: Medical trials, dynamic pricing, and procurement require identifying optimal decisions under hard resource budgets, not just maximizing cumulative reward
problem_framing: Extension of BAI (best arm identification) to resource-constrained setting; optimal arms are those in LP's optimal solution with positive value
key_insight: Complexity measure H bridges point-aspect (suboptimality of arms) and global-aspect (feasible domain structure); successive elimination-style algorithms 'veer widely from the optimal distribution'
method_signature: BASEOAK/FULLOAK with quarter reject/accept phases; FULLOAK has two-step: first converge to LP-optimal distribution, then eliminate arms
evaluation_criteria: Probability of correctly identifying all optimal arms before violating any resource knapsack constraint
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: 'The 'successive elimination-style' algorithm places excessive emphasis on point aspect and veers widely from the optimal distribution. BASEOAK cannot delete any optimal arm during the game, so the exploration ability is limited.'
thinking_moves: Identify why existing BAI methods fail under knapsack constraints: uniform exploration deviates from optimal distribution
Bridge two previously separate problem classes (BAI and BwK) through a unified complexity measure based on vertex gaps
Critique own BASEOAK algorithm as insufficient, motivate improved FULLOAK with two-phase approach
